intro: Four views of one idea. Ratios: a line adds the same amount over equal steps, an exponential multiplies by the same factor, and the exponential always wins in the end. Inverse: $y = \log_b x$ is $y = b^x$ reflected in $y = x$; every point swaps its coordinates. Log rules: heights on the graph of a log add when the inputs multiply. Semi-log: plot $\log_{10} y$ instead of $y$ and exponential data fall on a line whose slope and intercept give the model.
howItWorks:
• Ratios. $L(x) = a + mx$ and $E(x) = a \cdot b^x$ start at the same value. The table lists each step's difference (for $L$, always $m$) and ratio (for $E$, always $b$). Tap a step on the graph or in the table: it is marked in both.
  • Inverse. Drag the point on $y = b^x$; its mirror image on $y = \log_b x$ has the coordinates swapped. Reflect folds one graph onto the other.
  • Log rules. The product rule $\log_b(uv) = \log_b u + \log_b v$: the bar at $uv$ is as tall as the bars at $u$ and $v$ stacked. The quotient rule subtracts; the power rule stacks $k$ copies.
  • Semi-log. If $y = a \cdot b^x$, then $\log_{10} y = \log_{10} a + x \log_{10} b$: a line with slope $\log_{10} b$ and intercept $\log_{10} a$. The fit is least squares on $\log_{10} y$; $a$ and $b$ are shown to three decimals.
  • Keyboard: every slider and the draggable point move with the arrow keys.
